title: Applied anatomy: the rectum and anal canal (haemorrhoids, fistula, sphincters)

guidelineVersions: Parks et al., Br J Surg (1976)
ESCP anal fistula guideline, Colorectal Dis (2024)

brief.role: Core surgical trainee in the colorectal clinic
brief.scenario: Mr Robert Hughes, 52, has bright red bleeding after defecation and a lump that prolapses on straining, which he pushes back himself. He has been constipated for two years. The examiner will ask you about the anatomy of the rectum and anal canal, and will read out descriptions of anal fistula tracks.
brief.task: Answer the examiner's questions on the anatomy of the rectum and anal canal, and relate it to haemorrhoids, fistula-in-ano and continence.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Canal, sphincters, pectinate line; then cushions, fistula types and continence.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Calling haemorrhoids varicose veins of the portal system.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "The anal canal runs from the anorectal junction at puborectalis to the anal verge, about 4 cm."

grid.label: Rectum and canal
grid.fail: Cannot say where the anal canal begins or ends.
grid.pass: Rectum from the rectosigmoid junction (about S3) to the anorectal junction at puborectalis; anal canal about 4 cm to the anal verge.
grid.high: Adds puborectalis slings the junction forward to form the anorectal angle; rectum has no taeniae, haustra or appendices epiploicae.

grid.label: Sphincters
grid.fail: Calls the internal sphincter voluntary, or mixes up the two sphincters.
grid.pass: Internal: thickened circular smooth muscle, involuntary, gives resting tone. External: striated, voluntary, supplied by the pudendal nerve.
grid.high: Adds the conjoint longitudinal muscle in the intersphincteric plane, and the rectoanal inhibitory reflex relaxing the internal sphincter on rectal distension.

grid.label: Pectinate line
grid.fail: Cannot explain why lesions above the line are painless.
grid.pass: Above: columnar, autonomic nerves, superior rectal vessels, internal iliac and mesenteric nodes. Below: squamous, somatic nerves, inferior rectal vessels, inguinal nodes.
grid.high: Applies it: banding above the line is painless; tumours below the line spread to inguinal nodes.

grid.label: Anal cushions
grid.fail: Calls haemorrhoids varicose veins caused by portal hypertension.
grid.pass: Normal submucosal cushions (vessels, smooth muscle, connective tissue) in the left lateral, right anterior and right posterior positions; haemorrhoids are cushions that slide down.
grid.high: Explains sliding cushions: straining breaks down supporting tissue; bright red arterial bleeding from arteriovenous communications; grade by prolapse.

grid.label: Fistula classification
grid.fail: Cannot classify a fistula by its relation to the sphincters.
grid.pass: Parks: intersphincteric, trans-sphincteric, suprasphincteric, extrasphincteric; states how much external sphincter each crosses.
grid.high: Adds cryptoglandular origin from anal glands in the intersphincteric plane, and MRI to define complex tracks before surgery.

grid.label: Goodsall's rule
grid.fail: States the rule backwards, or cannot use it to predict the internal opening.
grid.pass: Transverse line across the anus: anterior external openings track straight radially; posterior openings curve to an internal opening in the posterior midline.
grid.high: Knows anterior openings far from the anal verge may also curve posteriorly; the rule guides, examination under anaesthesia or MRI confirms.

grid.label: Continence and surgery
grid.fail: Plans to lay open any fistula without considering how much sphincter it crosses.
grid.pass: Lays open low fistulas; for high trans-sphincteric fistulas uses a seton or sphincter-sparing repair to protect continence.
grid.high: Names advancement flap and LIFT; extra caution with anterior fistulas in women and previous obstetric sphincter injury.

fail.text: Where does the anal canal begin and end?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: It's the last part of the rectum, I'm not sure of the exact landmarks.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: The internal sphincter is the voluntary one you squeeze with.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I think it's done under local anaesthetic.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Varicose veins of the rectum, caused by back pressure in the portal system.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Describe the rectum and anal canal.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: The rectum runs from the rectosigmoid junction, about S3, to the anorectal junction where puborectalis slings round it. The anal canal is about 4 cm long, to the anal verge.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: The internal sphincter is thickened circular smooth muscle. It's involuntary and gives resting tone. The external sphincter is striated and voluntary, supplied by the pudendal nerve.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: What is the significance of the pectinate line?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Above it: columnar epithelium, autonomic supply, superior rectal vessels, drainage to internal iliac and mesenteric nodes. Below it: squamous, somatic nerves, inferior rectal vessels and inguinal nodes.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Normal anal cushions of vessels, muscle and connective tissue, in the left lateral, right anterior and right posterior positions. Haemorrhoids are cushions that have slid down.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Parks: intersphincteric, trans-sphincteric, suprasphincteric and extrasphincteric, by how much external sphincter the tract crosses.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Draw a transverse line across the anus. Anterior openings run straight in. Posterior openings curve to the posterior midline.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: How would you treat a high trans-sphincteric fistula?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Not by laying it open. I'd use a seton or a sphincter-sparing repair to protect continence.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Describe the rectum and anal canal.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Rectosigmoid junction at about S3 to the anorectal junction. Puborectalis pulls that junction forward to make the anorectal angle, which helps continence. The rectum has no taeniae, haustra or appendices epiploicae. The anal canal is about 4 cm long.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Internal sphincter: smooth, involuntary, resting tone. External: striated, voluntary, pudendal nerve. The conjoint longitudinal muscle lies in the intersphincteric plane. Rectal distension relaxes the internal sphincter: the rectoanal inhibitory reflex, which lets the canal sample contents.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Why does the pectinate line matter clinically?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Above it the supply is autonomic, so I can band there painlessly. Below it lymph drains to the inguinal nodes, so I'd examine the groins in a low anal cancer.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: They are anal cushions that have slid down. Straining breaks down the muscle and connective tissue that anchor them. The bleeding is bright red because it comes from arteriovenous communications. I grade them by prolapse; his reduce manually.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Most arise from infected anal glands in the intersphincteric plane. Parks classifies them as intersphincteric, trans-sphincteric, suprasphincteric or extrasphincteric. I'd get an MRI for anything complex before operating.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Anterior openings run radially, posterior ones curve to the midline. Anterior openings far from the verge can also curve backwards, so I'd confirm at examination under anaesthesia.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Lay open low fistulas. For high trans-sphincteric: seton, advancement flap or LIFT. I'd be especially careful with an anterior fistula in a woman or after obstetric sphincter injury.

failures.consequence: Misunderstands the disease and the basis of banding and haemorrhoidectomy.

failures.move: Laying open a high trans-sphincteric fistula.
failures.consequence: Divides much of the external sphincter and risks faecal incontinence.

failures.move: Not knowing the pectinate line divides visceral from somatic supply.
failures.consequence: Cannot explain painless banding or where anal cancer spreads.
Probes in the wrong place and risks a false passage.

recovery.line: Haemorrhoids are normal anal cushions that have slid down, not varicose veins.

recovery.when: Asked how to treat a fistula
recovery.line: First I need to know how much sphincter it crosses.

knowledge.fact: Anal canal: about 4 cm from the anorectal junction to the anal verge.
Internal sphincter: involuntary smooth muscle, resting tone. External: striated, voluntary, pudendal nerve.
Above the pectinate line: autonomic, painless; below: somatic, inguinal nodes.
Haemorrhoids are displaced anal cushions (sliding anal cushion concept).
Complex fistulas: MRI, and sphincter-sparing treatment to protect continence.

recall.think: Continence: how much sphincter would surgery divide?
recall.trap: Calling haemorrhoids portal varices; laying open high fistulas.
recall.finish: Low fistula: lay open. High: seton or sphincter-sparing repair.

partner.opening: Mr Hughes has bleeding and a prolapsing lump. Where does the anal canal begin and end?

reveals.finding: Ask: in a coronal section of the anal canal, two muscle layers surround the canal, separated by a thin plane. The inner layer is a pale, thickened continuation of the circular muscle of the rectum; the outer layer is striated muscle that is continuous above with levator ani. Name each layer, its nerve supply and whether it is voluntary, and the plane between them.
Proctoscopy: engorged cushions in the left lateral, right anterior and right posterior positions, prolapsing on straining.

Read out: a coronal diagram shows a fistula track running from an internal opening at the pectinate line, through both the internal and the external sphincter below the level of puborectalis, then down through the ischioanal fossa to an external opening on the perianal skin. Classify it.
Read out: a perineal diagram, patient in lithotomy, with a transverse line drawn across the centre of the anus. The external opening is at 5 o'clock, 2 cm from the verge.

push.question: Where does the anal canal begin and end?
push.expect: Anorectal junction at puborectalis to anal verge; about 4 cm.

push.question: In a sagittal section of the anorectum, a U-shaped sling of muscle passes behind the bowel at the junction of the rectum and anal canal and pulls it forwards. What is it, and what does it create?
push.expect: Puborectalis; it forms the anorectal angle at the anorectal junction, which helps continence.

push.question: In the same section, a wavy line of small mucosal folds joins the lower ends of the vertical mucosal columns, about halfway down the anal canal. What is it, and what changes across it?
push.expect: Pectinate line: columnar and autonomic above, squamous and somatic below; superior versus inferior rectal vessels; mesenteric and internal iliac versus inguinal nodes.

push.question: Why is banding painless?
push.expect: Above the pectinate line: autonomic supply.

push.question: What are haemorrhoids?
push.expect: Displaced anal cushions; not portal varices.

push.question: Where is the internal opening of this posterior fistula?
How would you treat a high trans-sphincteric fistula?
push.expect: Seton or sphincter-sparing repair; not fistulotomy.

curveballs.prompt: He has cirrhosis. Does that explain his haemorrhoids?
curveballs.safeAnswer: No. Haemorrhoids are displaced anal cushions; rectal varices in portal hypertension are a different condition.

curveballs.prompt: What is the rectoanal inhibitory reflex?
curveballs.safeAnswer: Rectal distension relaxes the internal sphincter so the upper canal can sample contents; mediated by the intramural nerve plexus.

curveballs.prompt: A woman has an anterior trans-sphincteric fistula after a difficult delivery. Can you lay it open?
curveballs.safeAnswer: No. The anterior sphincter is short and may already be damaged; MRI and a sphincter-sparing option.
